name: Ambakich
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: read SIL PNG endangered-language listing for Ambakich (no phonology); only sociolinguistic survey + wordlists exist

sources.citation: Barlow, Russell. 2021. Ambakich phonological sketch. Language and Linguistics in Oceania 13: 32-88. (open PDF athttps://www.izumi-syuppan.co.jp/LLO_PDF/vol_13/13-03.pdf)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. The paper describes itself as 'an account of Ambakich segmental phonology' (p.32, p.34): phoneme inventory (2.1), phonetic realizations (2.2), consonants (2.3), vowels incl. reduction of vowels in open/word-final syllables (2.4), syllable structure (2.5), then word lists. The strings stress/accent/tone/suprasegmental/prosody do not occur anywhere in the 57 pages; no stress marks in the transcriptions.

sources.citation: Barlow, Russell. 2023. A grammar of Ulwa (Papua New Guinea). (Comprehensive Grammar Library) Berlin: Language Science Press. [checked only for what it says about Ambakich]
sources.note: Mentions Ambakich only for classification, loans and cognate sets (citing Barlow 2021 and Potter et al. 2008 as the only sources on the language); nothing on Ambakich stress.

sources.citation: Barlow, Russell. 2020. A sketch grammar of Pondi. (Asia-Pacific Linguistics) Canberra: ANU Press. [checked only for Ambakich mentions]
sources.note: Ambakich appears only in Keram pronoun/cognate tables and classification discussion; nothing on Ambakich stress.

sources.citation: Potter, Margaret, Philip Lambrecht, Laura Aleman & Correna Janzen. 2008. The sociolinguistic situation of the Ambakich language. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2008-012. SIL International. 86 pp. (https://www.sil.org/resources/archives/8990;PDF obtained via web.archive.org snapshot of the SIL file URL)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3.4 'Characteristics of the Language' gives only consonant and vowel phone charts from wordlist elicitation and SOV word order; Appendix H wordlists (5 villages) are in a legacy phonetic font; no statement about stress or tone. The only hit for 'accent' (p.5) is a Tok Pisin remark about dialect prestige.

sources.citation: Barlow, Russell. In preparation/forthcoming work on Ambakich grammar or comparative Keram (author states further grammatical research is needed, Barlow 2021: 75; Glottolog 5.3 cites 'Barlow 2023: 24-28' = Ulwa grammar for Keram subclassification only).

sources.note: Barlow is the only linguist with recent Ambakich field data (2018, Yaut); any fuller sketch by him would be the first source able to state stress placement.
